fallthrough_behavior_traced.what_happens_when_a_gate_rejects_a_claim: status is reset to 'no_match', matched_alpha/matched_alpha_name reset to None. No second-ranked candidate is selected, no fallback classifier is invoked, no top-k re-ranking occurs, and no other Alpha's candidate entry is touched. The claim becomes genuinely unmatched.
fallthrough_behavior_traced.code_evidence: candidates/eligible_candidates/top/second/ambiguous-detection are all computed via the deterministic _candidate_score() layer BEFORE either new gate runs, and are never recomputed or mutated afterward -- confirmed by direct inspection of map_claim_to_alpha's control flow.
fallthrough_behavior_traced.graph_builder_evidence: graph_engine/graph_builder.py::_committed_alpha_ids_for_claim() reads a single, exclusive matched_alpha per claim_id. When a claim's matched_alpha becomes None, the function returns [] for that claim -- the associated graph edge is marked with a reason code (e.g. NO_COMMITTED_ALPHA_MATCH), never silently re-attributed to a different Alpha. A claim can only ever be committed to the one Alpha its own matched_alpha field names, so no other Alpha's local_structure_support can gain evidence from a rejected A001 claim.
fallthrough_behavior_traced.conclusion: Rejecting an A001 match cannot redirect that claim's evidence into another Alpha, at either the Alpha Mapper layer or the graph-edge/local-structure-support layer.
